Godrej Consumer Products Limited has informed the Exchange that according to the Company's stock options plan (GCLP ESOP), options are granted out of shares acquired by means of subscription or secondary market purchase by an independent trust funded by the Company, in terms of the special resolutions passed by the shareholders on March 14, 2007 and April 24, 2008. In terms of the powers vested in the Board of Directors by the aforesaid shareholders' resolutions, the Board has in its meeting held on December 15, 2009, modified clause 5.7(c) of GCPL ESOP, which lays down the vesting date in case of retirement of employees. The clause 5.7(c) prior to modification and the modified clause 5.7(c) is reproduced below for reference: Clause prior to modification: " In the event of separation from employment for reasons of normal Retirement or Retirement specifically approved by a Participating Company, (i) all Vested Options should be Exercised by the Option Grantee immediately after, but in no event later than six months from the date of such Option Grantee's Retirement, (ii) all Unvested Options will lapse as on the date of such Retirement, unless otherwise determined by the Compensation Committee and which determination will be final and binding. Modified Clause- "In the event of separation from employment for reasons of normal Retirement or Retirement specifically approved by a Participating Company, (i) all Unvested Options shall vest in the employee on the date of retirement or at an earlier date as may be decided by the Compensation Committee, subject to the requirement of minimum vesting period specified in clause 5.4 of the GCPL ESOP (ii) all Vested Options should be Exercised by the Option Grantee on retirement, but in no event later than six months from the date of such Option Grantee's Retirement." The modified clause will be applicable for all unvested options as on date and for all options granted henceforth.

This is on a rating scale of CGR1 to CGR6 where CGR1 denotes the highest rating. The + sign indicates a relatively higher standing within the category indicated by the rating. The CGR2+ rating implies that in ICRA's current opinion, the rated Company has adopted and follows such practices, conventions and codes as would provide its financial stakeholders a high level of assurance on the quality of corporate governance. 2) Rating for Stakeholder Value and Governance Practices: ICRA has reaffirmed the SVG2+ (pronounced as SVG 2 plus) rating for Stakeholders Value Creation and Governance practices of the Company. This is on a rating scale of SVG1 to SVG6 where SVG1 denotes the highest rating. The + sign indicates a relatively higher standing within the category indicated by the rating. The SVG2+ rating implies that in ICRA's current opinion, the rated Company belongs to the High Category on the composite parameters of stakeholder value creation and management as also corporate governance practices.

Godrej Consumer Products Limited has informed the Exchange that they have received intimations from two of its Promoters viz. Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company Limited (G&B) and Godrej Industries Limited (GIL) that there was an inter-se transfer of 22,25,000 equity shares (3.93% of the total capital) from G&B to GIL. The details of the same are as follows : 1) Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company Limited has sold 22,25,000 shares representing 3.93% of the paid up capital of Godrej Consumer Products Limited. The date of sale is November 02, 2004 and the mode of sale is Inter-se transfer to 'Group' Company viz. Godrej Industries Ltd., under Regulations 3(1)(e)(i) of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares & Takeovers) Regulations 1997, on the Stock Exchange, Mumbai. The shareholding of Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company Limited after the said sale is 2,53,42,522 shares representing 44.77% of the paid up capital of Godrej Consumer Products Limited. 2) Godrej Industries Limited has acquired 22,25,000 shares representing 3.93% of the paid up capital of Godrej Consumer Products Limited. The date of acquisition is November 02, 2004 and the mode of acquisition is Inter-se transfer from 'Group' Company viz. Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company Limited, under Regulations 3(1)(e)(i) of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares & Takeovers) Regulations 1997, on the Stock Exchange, Mumbai. The shareholding of Godrej Industries Limited after the said acquisition is 71,25,000 shares representing 12.59% of the paid up capital of Godrej Consumer Products Limited. Clarification of News : The press had reports that Godrej Consumer Products Limited has shown a keen interest to acquire the brands of Paras Pharmaceuticals.  The Exchange, in order to verify the accuracy or otherwise of the information reported in the press and to inform the market place so that the interest of the investors is safeguarded, had written to the officials of the company.
